# `kernel/ledger/FinalReport.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/ledger/FinalReport.js`

FinalReport.js — assembles the end-of-task report for one AI request from the ledger's parts: goal outcome, task summary, tool/resource/sampling/ elicitation activity, blockers hit, receipts issued. This is what the overlay shows when a task completes and what gets persisted with the request record.

## Functions

### `projectArtifactToolFailureDiagnostic(value = {})`

Convert an Artifact mutation failure into a fixed, content-free diagnostic. Raw handler text is used only to select a known category and is never returned, so prompts, file contents, tool arguments, and provider bodies cannot enter Run Details or copied diagnostics through this path.

### `projectProviderFailureDiagnostic(value)`

Keep only broker-authored, content-free failure evidence. Provider payloads, prompts, credentials, endpoints, and response bodies are deliberately absent.

### `projectNaviModelRouteBlocker(value)`

Preserve a content-free model compatibility decision when the kernel stops before provider dispatch. This is intentionally separate from `modelExecution`: zero attempts is evidence that no provider was called.

### `projectModelExecutionDiagnostic(value)`

Project a Navi broker execution into a bounded diagnostic receipt. Request hashes and partial-result hashes are intentionally excluded because they can fingerprint operator content without helping an operator diagnose routing.

### `publicErrorNumberForFailure({ errorCode = '', failure = null } = {})`

### `createAIIncidentId(requestId)`

### `projectAIEchoPipelineTrace(value, { requestId = '', incidentId = null, outcome = '', errorCode = null, errorNumber = null, openedAt = 0, closedAt = 0, synthesizeTerminal = true, } = {})`

Project the existing resumable run stream into one compact, durable, content-free diagnostic trace. This is deliberately a report projection, not a second event registry or ledger. Unknown fields are dropped rather than recursively scrubbed so prompts, provider bodies, credentials, raw tool arguments, and reasoning deltas cannot cross this boundary.

### `projectAIEchoLivePipelineTrace(value, { requestId = '', openedAt = 0, } = {})`

Project an open run through the same content-free allowlist as FinalReport without inventing a terminal event. Live trajectory UI is a view over the kernel stream, not a second ledger, and therefore cannot claim completion.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
